description:
Isolated during the fz-kdt.108 landing (2026-09-02, coordinator's own
clean FIFO/LIFO measurement, distinct-md5 binaries): 00277_enum_tier0_fixture
stays schedule-visible at 562 backend-canon lines base AND head (fz-kdt.108
closed enum_map_family 1170->0 but not this). Root: fz-kdt.108's canonical
construction-wrapper order keys on Types::cmp_tys(surface.inputs), and
cmp_tys' free-var tiebreak (types/order.rs::cmp_var) falls back to raw
TypeVarId mint order (a.0.cmp(&b.0)) -- which is schedule-sensitive. 00277's
(int, list(int | :tail)) surfaces tie structurally, so their order (and the
activation-key Tys minted from it) follows a schedule-unstable key. This is
the ONE documented residual of the whole cmp_ty canonical instrument
(kdt.101/105/129 all noted it and were unaffected because their inputs had no
free-var ties). BEHAVIOR-NEUTRAL (00277 stdout identical 3 doors both
schedules; the 562 lines are exec-count 180 vs 181 + return-field marshaling,
never output). Also entangled with fz-kdt.107 (00277's 3-arm dispatch-twin
clause-order class) -- the review recorded 00277 as BOTH; determine which
component the free-var key closes vs which is 107's. FIX DIRECTION: give
cmp_var a schedule-stable free-var key -- a content-derived / address-path
key, not raw TypeVarId (the same lesson as StableSortKey for activation
arrows, fz-k22.21). Sequence: measure 00277's residual again after fz-kdt.107
lands, then close whatever free-var-tie component remains.

comments.text: CROSS-SESSION WITNESS folded from fz-kdt.174 (2026-09-02): the same base binary (8c3d5ce90) compiled 00277_enum_tier0_fixture to two different backend programs in two sessions/worktrees (md5 cafaf7f6.. 3 dispatch nodes/180 executables vs dc9a2fc7.. 2/181; 571 diff lines: shifted entry id, w6/w7 construction swaps on Enum.reduce/3#lambda, whole vs fields(whole,whole) return demand, an extra Enum.reverse/2#lambda target per row) while 17 same-session runs were stable. This is the 180-vs-181 residue this ticket already owns (free-var tiebreak on TypeVarId mint order + fz-kdt.124's dbg[empty_list()] key): the instability is cross-process, so the fix must be a content-derived key, and the acceptance is cross-process md5 stability of 00277's dump, not same-session.

THESIS REFUTED BY PROBE at d2a5f3510 (2026-09-02). An eprintln in types/order.rs cmp_var's (None, None) arm -- the TypeVarId mint-order fallback this ticket names as 00277's root -- fires ZERO times on 00277 under FIFO and under LIFO, and zero times on every one of the 597 corpus fixtures under FIFO. Equal-key neighbours after the two cmp_tys wrapper/direct-edge sorts (jobs/runtime_demand.rs :1271 and :3206): none on 00277 under either schedule. The free-var tie is not what moves this fixture.

WHAT DOES MOVE IT (head FIFO vs head LIFO canon, 571 lines, key-set and return-form diff):
  LIFO only: Kernel.dbg/1[empty_list()] and Kernel.fz_dbg_value/1[empty_list()], both `return any`; main/0 `return any` (FIFO: list(int)).
  LIFO only: Enum.reverse/2[impl-target::Range | {int,int,int} | %{...}, non_empty_list(:tail)] `return empty_list()` (FIFO: list(int)).
  FIFO only: Range.reduce/5[int, int, int, {:cont, empty_list()}, closure[Enum.reduce/3#lambda](closure[Enum.reverse/2#lambda]())] returning {:done, list(int)}.
  Everything else in the 571 lines is renumbering (x180/x181, w6/w7, w14/w15) downstream of that key-set difference.
This is fz-kdt.120's family: `dbg([])` returns `any` because arrow_match.rs drops a @spec variable bound to the whole `[]` argument (fz-f98.16's "ambiguous empty list" drop), and the join-only return ladder (fz-kdt.65) keeps whichever intermediate a schedule happened to publish. The `[]`-keyed activations that exist under one schedule only are fz-kdt.124's contained-key question. Re-measure this fixture after 120 lands; this ticket's cmp_var change is not on the path to 00277's confluence and should not be built for it.
